chunks: Then he sent to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and said

to him the same as what he had said to the Qureyshi. Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you see that if I do not accept you, will you not kill me just as you killed the man yesterday?' Yazeed (may Allah curse him) said to him, 'Yes.' So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'I have accepted to you with what you asked. I am a compelled slave, so if you wish, detain me, and if you wish, sell me.' So Yazeed (may Allah curse him) said to him: 'It is of a higher level for you; I spare your blood, and that will not diminish your nobility.'

key_terms.الرَّجُلَ: The man (referring to the person killed the previous day)
key_terms.لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ: May Allah curse him (a common honorific/curse formula in Shia texts)

ai.seo_question: What did Ali ibn al-Husayn say to Yazeed to avoid being killed?
ai.summary: This narration, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the political and spiritual dynamics between the Umayyad Caliph Yazeed and Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) following the Battle of Karbala. By offering himself as a slave, the Imam demonstrates a pragmatic acceptance of his captivity while asserting his inherent nobility, to which Yazeed concedes that sparing his life will not diminish his status. This exchange underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Ahl al-Bayt's dignified endurance under political oppression, contrasting their spiritual superiority with the temporal power of the Umayyads.
